articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 200 security patches in one Patch Tuesday, with nearly three dozen rated 'critical' — because apparently they've been saving up all year like it's Christmas morning for vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle zero-day to ransack American universities like digital pirates with a treasure map. Higher education just got a very expensive lesson in enterprise security.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702 surveillance authority has finally expired! The NSA's favorite backdoor into American communications just got slammed shut, at least temporarily.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like leaving nuclear codes in a public bathroom. Congress is predictably having a meltdown over the cybersecurity agency's own cybersecurity fail.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: Splunk Enterprise gets pwned by a critical 9.8 CVSS flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Your log analysis tool just became someone else's backdoor.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits. Even the DIY Linux crowd isn't safe from supply chain attacks.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Chinese hackers backdoored Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, hiding in plain sight inside the login system itself. The ultimate example of why you should never trust your authentication stack.

articles.title: The new BitLocker exploit everyone's freaking out about probably won't affect you
articles.summary: Autonomous security agent discovers 21 zero-days in FFmpeg after Google and Anthropic missed them. AI vs AI — at least someone's putting these models to good use finding bugs instead of writing poetry.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle warns of security bug exploited in mass-hacking campaign affecting 100+ organizations. When Oracle actually bothers to warn you quickly, you know it's bad.

articles.title: ICE Should Show It Hasn’t Been “Infiltrated by Violent Extremists,” Senator Urges
articles.summary: Indiana bans press from executions claiming 'dignity' — but secret state-sanctioned killing serves repression, not dignity. Transparency dies in darkness, literally.
